summary: This is a general overview entry: 'Vaccine' is a class of active immunizing biological agents rather than a single product. Vaccines contain antigens (live-attenuated organisms, inactivated organisms, subunits, toxoids, polysaccharides/conjugates, or nucleic acid/mRNA platforms) that stimulate the immune system to develop protective, often long-lasting, immunity against a specific infection. Dose, route, schedule, age range, contraindications, and storage are entirely product-specific. Always select the exact vaccine product and consult its prescribing information and the national/ACIP/WHO immunization schedule before administration.
indications: Active immunization to prevent specific infectious diseases (product-dependent)
Primary immunization series and booster doses per the recommended schedule
Pre-exposure or post-exposure prophylaxis for certain vaccines (e.g., rabies, tetanus, hepatitis B)

dosage.d: Follow the exact dose, volume, and schedule in the specific vaccine's prescribing information
dosage.n: Do not generalize dosing across vaccines

dosage.d: One or more doses at defined intervals
dosage.n: Complete the full series for protection

admin: Confirm the exact vaccine product, formulation, dose, and route before administration
Verify storage/cold-chain integrity and expiry; reconstitute correctly if required
Screen for contraindications and precautions (allergy, immunocompromise, pregnancy for live vaccines)
Administer by the labeled route (commonly intramuscular or subcutaneous) and observe for immediate reactions
Document lot number, site, date, and provide the next-dose schedule
moa: Vaccines introduce antigen (whole organism, subunit, toxoid, polysaccharide/conjugate, or nucleic acid encoding an antigen) to the immune system, which mounts an adaptive response generating antigen-specific antibodies and memory B and T cells. On later exposure to the real pathogen, this immune memory enables a rapid, protective response that prevents or attenuates disease. Adjuvants in some vaccines enhance the immune response.

absolute: Severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) to a previous dose or to a vaccine component
Live-attenuated vaccines in significant immunocompromise and (generally) in pregnancy
relative: Moderate to severe acute illness (defer until recovery)
Recent receipt of certain biologics/blood products (may affect live-vaccine response)
Specific product precautions per its label
monitor: Immediate hypersensitivity for at least 15 minutes after administration
Vaccine-specific precautions in the product label

preg: Inactivated, subunit, toxoid, and many recommended vaccines (e.g., influenza, Tdap, certain others) are generally considered safe and are recommended in pregnancy. Live-attenuated vaccines are generally avoided during pregnancy. Always follow the specific vaccine's labeling and current obstetric immunization guidance.
lact: Most vaccines, including live vaccines for the mother, are generally compatible with breastfeeding. Follow the specific product's labeling for any exceptions.
renal: No dosage adjustment is generally needed; however, response may be reduced in patients with significant immunocompromise (including some renal/dialysis patients), and additional or higher-dose schedules may apply per product guidance.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is generally needed; immune response may be reduced in significant immunocompromise per product guidance.

major: Immunosuppressive therapy (high-dose corticosteroids, chemotherapy, biologics) - reduced response and contraindication to live vaccines
moderate: Other vaccines - some require spacing of live vaccines (e.g., 4 weeks apart) per guidance
Antiviral drugs - may reduce response to certain live vaccines (e.g., varicella, influenza nasal)
minor: Antipyretics around vaccination - prophylactic use may slightly lower antibody response
interactions.food: Generally not relevant; some oral vaccines have specific feeding restrictions per label.
interactions.diagnostics: Some live vaccines can transiently affect tuberculin/IGRA testing - follow timing guidance.

serious: Vaccine-specific severe reactions per product labeling
rare: Febrile seizure (in young children, certain vaccines)
emergency: Anaphylaxis (difficulty breathing, swelling, collapse) - treat with epinephrine

Local and systemic reactions in the following days
Completion of the recommended dose series

pearls: Group/ambiguous entry: 'Vaccine' is a drug class, not one product - always select the specific vaccine and follow its prescribing information and the national/ACIP/WHO schedule
Platform matters: live-attenuated vaccines are generally avoided in pregnancy and immunocompromise; inactivated/subunit/mRNA are not live
Anaphylaxis is rare but possible - have epinephrine available and observe after administration
Cold-chain integrity is critical; check storage temperature and expiry before use
Document lot number, site, and route; complete the full series for protection
missed: If a scheduled dose in a vaccine series is missed or delayed, it generally does not require restarting the series - resume as soon as possible per the catch-up schedule for that vaccine. Follow the specific product and national immunization guidance.
overdose: Inadvertent administration of an extra dose of most vaccines is generally not harmful but may increase local and systemic reactions. Management is supportive. Report the error per local pharmacovigilance/immunization safety procedures and follow product-specific guidance. Treat any anaphylaxis immediately with epinephrine.
